cursor.description: Cursor-relative ordering, when `at` was supplied and the chronology is acyclic.

cycle.description: Cycle blame edges, if the chronology is cyclic.

layers.description: Topological layers; empty when the chronology is cyclic.

placements.description: Episode fact placements projected onto story-time.

CyclePos.description:
A position on a cycle.

Not `Ord`: a cycle refuses rank, so two positions are never `<`-compared. The
`index` is a congruence class modulo the cycle's length — an out-of-range
value is normalized by navigation, never rejected mid-walk.

cycle.description: The cycle this position belongs to.

index.description: The spoke index (read modulo the cycle's length).

EpisodeAnchor.description:
Where an episode or scene sits in story-time.

An anchor names an [`era`](Self::era) membership and, *within* that era, an
honestly-partial position pinned by [`after`](Self::after) /
[`before`](Self::before) event constraints (there is no offset — an
undeclared pair is unordered). It may also bind cyclic [`phases`](Self::phases)
— a tide, a moon-night, a season — one [`CyclePos`] per relevant cycle.

The [`Default`] (empty) anchor is *unanchored*: an unanchored episode follows
its predecessor in the story-present, the current behavior preserved. A
scene's own anchor, when present, overrides its episode's ([`Scene::scene_anchor`]).

after.description: Events this anchor falls strictly after (intra-era precedence).

before.description: Events this anchor falls strictly before (intra-era precedence).

era.description: The era this anchor sits in, if declared.

phases.description: Cyclic phase coordinates at this story point, one per cycle.

EraRef.description: A reference to an era on the chronology spine, by name.

EventRef.description: A reference to a named event (a point on the timeline), by name.

FactRef.description: A reference to a fact the world may hold, by name.

Placement.description: One fact-introduction, resolved onto its story-time placement by the fold.

anchor.description: Where in story-time the fact was so (scene anchor, else episode anchor).

production_order.description: The production slot that introduced it (the listener's when).

TimelineCursor.description: The relation of every known point to a requested cursor.

unordered.description: Points with no declared order relative to it.

TimelineLayer.description: One topological layer in a chronology.

points.description: Era and event names in this layer.
